question: Where can I get the routes (geometry) of hydrogen pipelines in operation or planned in the United States, with operator, capacity and status?

answer.summary: PHMSA's NPMS has restricted GIS data for reported hydrogen transmission lines. Texas RRC offers public line geometry. Its name filter identifies candidate hydrogen segments and can miss or misclassify lines. PHMSA annual reports give operators and mileage without routes. Capacity per pipeline was not verified. Angeles Link documentation contains preliminary corridors.
main_caveats: PHMSA limits access to the NPMS GIS data. Its public viewer shows county-level selections.
Texas RRC files hydrogen as 'OTHER GAS'; hydrogen lines are identified only by names containing H2/HYDROGEN, so some lines may be missed or mixed with other gases.
Capacity per pipeline was not found in the sources checked. Diameter and annual operator volume measure different attributes.
Angeles Link materials show preliminary corridors. CPUC decision D.26-04-034 denied ratepayer cost recovery for Phase 2 engineering and design studies.
Blends (Hawaii SNG with 10-12% H2 in service; California pilots of 0.1-20% pending) are not dedicated hydrogen pipelines; no US conversion of a gas line to 100% hydrogen was found.
answer.confidence_reason: Texas, PHMSA, NPMS and Louisiana checks were tested; PHMSA and operator sites block automated clients (PHMSA data read from an archived ZIP); IEA contents and planned projects outside California remain unverified.

attributes.note: Texas RRC has mapped lines that can be screened for hydrogen and checked with the RRC inventory. OSM has uneven coverage. Angeles Link shows preliminary corridors.
attributes.gap_note: Nationwide geometry is in NPMS (HG) but restricted to government/operators; no public layer for Louisiana (DCE links maps to NPMS) or other states.

attributes.note: National operator list from PHMSA reports; operator per segment only in Texas (RRC) and OSM; SoCalGas for Angeles Link.
attributes.gap_note: Operator per segment outside Texas is in NPMS, restricted; PHMSA reports give operator per report, not per pipeline.

attributes.note: Only a planned system design throughput (Angeles Link 1.5 MMT/Y). RRC gives diameter, PHMSA annual volume per operator; neither is capacity.
attributes.gap_note: No capacity field in RRC layer/list, NPMS dictionary or PHMSA form (Part C is volume transported); operator pages give network totals only.

attributes.note: Texas: In Service/Abandoned (layer), Active/Idle (list). Planned and blends: CPUC dockets (Angeles Link, pilots) and Hawaii PUC (10-12% H2 blend in service).
attributes.gap_note: NPMS status codes nationwide are restricted; IEA list of planned projects needs a login; no national list of planned lines opened.

caveats: Hydrogen filed as 'OTHER GAS' (OGT); name filtering is needed and imperfect.
RRC states GIS maps may not be used for pipeline location purposes.

coverage.geographic: Texas only (county files by FIPS code, statewide service); pipelines holding an RRC T-4 permit, including interstate segments inside Texas.

unit.value: DIAMETER in inches (outside diameter up to 12 in, nominal pipe size above); no capacity, pressure or flow field in the public layer.
unit.quote: Always use Outside Diameter unless the diameter is greater than 12 inches, then use Nominal Pipe Size.

inclusion_rule.value: Pipelines that require an RRC T-4 permit; hydrogen has no own commodity code and is filed as OGT 'Other Gas' transmission.

reference_date.value: County files dated 11/27/26 on the download share (file timestamps 2026-11-25 inside the ZIP); service has no per-record date.

update_frequency.value: Twice a week (digital map layers by county).
update_frequency.quote: Pipeline Layers by County ... ArcView Shape File ... Twice a week

exclusions.value: Not for locating pipelines on the ground; only In Service (active and idle) and Abandoned states, no planned lines; lines without H2/HYDROGEN in their names cannot be told apart from other gases.
exclusions.quote: GIS maps may not be used for pipeline location purposes.

key_fields.meaning: Operator name registered with RRC (P-5 operator).
Operator's system and subsystem names; the only place where 'H2' or 'HYDROGEN' identifies hydrogen service.
Commodity; hydrogen lines appear as 'OTHER GAS' (code OGT), one system as 'HYDROGEN'.
Pipe diameter in inches.
RRC T-4 permit number; join key with the RRC Hydrogen Pipelines list.
Yes/No (service) or Y/N (shapefile) interstate designation.
'In Service' (I: active and/or idle) or 'Abandoned' (B).
Texas county of the segment.

how_to_use.example_request: curl -sG "https://gis.rrc.texas.gov/server/rest/services/rrc_public/RRC_Public_Viewer_Srvs/MapServer/13/query" --data-urlencode "where=COMMODITY='HYDROGEN' OR ((SYSTEM_NAME LIKE '%HYDROGEN%' OR SUBSYSTEM_NAME LIKE '%HYDROGEN%' OR SYSTEM_NAME LIKE '%H2%' OR SUBSYSTEM_NAME LIKE '%H2%') AND COMMODITY='OTHER GAS')" --data-urlencode "returnCountOnly=true" --data-urlencode "f=json"
how_to_use.example_result: {"count":928}. With outFields and outSR=4326&f=geojson, e.g. OPERATOR "AIR LIQUIDE LARGE INDUST U.S. LP", SYSTEM_NAME "EAST TEXAS HYDROGEN", SUBSYSTEM_NAME "EAST TEXAS 20 INCH HYDROGEN", DIAMETER 20, T4PERMIT "08531", INTERSTATE "No", STATUS "In Service", COUNTY_NAME "JEFFERSON", LineString starting [-93.98838, 29.88017].
steps: Query layer 13 'Pipelines' of RRC_Public_Viewer_Srvs with the where clause above, outFields=OPERATOR,SYSTEM_NAME,SUBSYSTEM_NAME,DIAMETER,T4PERMIT,COMMODITY,INTERSTATE,STATUS,COUNTY_NAME, outSR=4326, f=geojson; maxRecordCount is 1000, so page with resultOffset if a filter returns more.

The name filter without the 'HYDROGEN' commodity returned 926 segments (902 In Service, 24 Abandoned; 622 interstate, 304 intrastate) in 13 counties; haversine length of the returned geometry is about 993 miles.

Alternative: download pipelineNNN.zip per county from the RRC download share (e.g. pipeline201.zip = Harris, 5,332,327 bytes, 8,667 segments) and filter SYS_NM/SUBSYS_NM/CMDTY_DESC the same way; the shapefile is NAD27 geographic.
Join T4PERMIT to the RRC Hydrogen Pipelines list (source rrc-tx-hydrogen-list) to separate RRC-recognised intrastate hydrogen accounts and their Active/Idle state.
Review the result by operator: industrial-gas operators also run CO, syngas, nitrogen and oxygen lines under OTHER GAS (Air Products 'TX - CO', 'TX - SG' in Harris).
reading_traps: Hydrogen is not a commodity code: 1,654 Texas segments are OTHER GAS and only those with H2/HYDROGEN in names are identifiable; Linde's 'GCPOC' system (304 mi in the filter) carries H2 only in subsystem names.
STATUS 'In Service' includes idle lines; the RRC Hydrogen Pipelines list marks some of the same permits as Idle (35.2 of 481.4 miles).
Text filter false positives exist in the shapefile (e.g. refined-product or HVL lines with 'H2' in a subsystem name); restrict to gas commodities.
Segment lengths: the shapefile field ALBERS_MIL is miles; the service SHAPE.LEN depends on the spatial reference; compute lengths yourself.
No planned or proposed lines: a segment appears only after a T-4 permit and mapping submission.

how_to_use.example_result: 1,470 reports, DATAFILE_AS_OF 5/1/2026, REPORT_YEAR 2025; 33 with PARTA5COMMODITY 'Hydrogen Gas', PARTDTTOTAL sum 1,612.242 mi. Row: 117, AIR PRODUCTS & CHEMICALS INC, PARTA7INTER 'LOUISIANA, TEXAS', PARTA7INTRA 'CALIFORNIA, OHIO, TEXAS', PARTDTTOTAL 610.393.
steps: Download the ZIP 'Gas Transmission & Gathering Annual Data - 2010 to present' (about 110 MB; 135 entries) from the PHMSA annual report data page.
Open 'GT AR <year> Part A to D.csv' (CSV, comma-separated) or annual_gas_transmission_gathering_<year>.xlsx and keep rows with PARTA5COMMODITY = 'Hydrogen Gas'.

Largest hydrogen reports for CY2025: Air Products & Chemicals (OPID 117) 610.393 mi, Linde (20044) 459.5 mi, Air Liquide Large Industries U.S. (842) 367.93 mi; 30 other refinery and chemical operators share the rest.
CY2025 hydrogen reports cover 11 states: Texas (20 reports), Louisiana (11), Washington (3), Ohio, Alabama, Utah (2 each), California, Indiana, New York, Oklahoma, Kansas (1 each).
For miles per state use Parts H-T, which the form fills once per state and per interstate/intrastate (fields STATE_NAME, INTER_INTRA).
Use OPERATOR_ID to match NPMS OPID and RRC/OSM operator names.
reading_traps: Part C is annual volume transported per operator, not pipeline capacity; Linde reports 418,069,399.74 against 326,179.27 for Air Products, an implausible value for million scf per year.
Report 'Hydrogen Gas' miles (1,612) match the DOE '1,600 miles' only at national level; there is no route or segment list.
Other Gas reports such as 'Other Gas-CO, H2, N2' (Centauri) carry hydrogen mixtures outside the Hydrogen Gas group.
The live PHMSA site returns 403 Access Denied to automated clients; the ZIP exceeds 100 MB.

if_unstructured.summary: Planned or proposed hydrogen pipelines have no structured source: status comes from state commission dockets and construction notices, routes only from operator study figures.
recipe: Operating lines outside Texas: take operators and states from PHMSA annual reports (PARTA5COMMODITY = 'Hydrogen Gas'), then request NPMS data through a government agency or use OSM ways for the same operators.
Texas operating lines: query the RRC layer with the H2/HYDROGEN filter and join T4PERMIT to the RRC Hydrogen Pipelines list for Active/Idle state.
Planned lines: check RRC PS-48 construction PDFs (Texas) and state commission dockets (CPUC for California) for filings; read the decision summary for phase and status.
Planned routes: read figure-based corridors in operator feasibility studies (Angeles Link sections 3.3.4 and 5.1); they cannot be digitised to more than corridor precision.
if_unstructured.location_method: Operating lines: RRC geometry (Texas) or OSM; elsewhere NPMS via an authorised agency. Planned lines: schematic study figures only, corridor precision.
